title: How do you build a training matrix for a SaaS company?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a SaaS company
description: Build a SaaS training matrix: GDPR, ISO 27001, AI Act, NIS2, PCI DSS, HIPAA and privacy duties by role and market, with frequency and evidence rules.
shortAnswer: A SaaS company training matrix maps engineering, support, sales, security and leadership roles against three kinds of obligation: data protection and AI laws in each market it sells into, certifications it holds such as ISO/IEC 27001 or PCI DSS, and duties passed down by customers, such as HIPAA business associate terms. Each cell records the source, the market, the refresh clock and the evidence an auditor or customer will request.
keyTakeaways: A SaaS firm's training columns come from three places: laws where its customers and data subjects are, certifications it chooses to hold, and obligations it inherits as a processor or business associate.
Most data protection laws imply training rather than mandate a course: GDPR, the UAE PDPL and the Australian Privacy Act all work through security and accountability duties.
Few sources fix a clock. PCI DSS requires the awareness program to be reviewed at least every 12 months; HIPAA privacy training is due at onboarding and after material policy changes.
AI features add rows: EU AI Act Article 4 requires measures to support the AI literacy of staff who build or use AI systems, and ISO/IEC 42001 adds competence and awareness clauses.
Enterprise customers and certification auditors ask for competence evidence and retained records, so the matrix should store the evidence rule alongside each duty.

sections.heading: Where do a SaaS company's training obligations come from?

blocks.text: They come from the markets the company sells into, the certifications it holds, and the roles it plays in its customers' compliance, not from a single industry regulator. A SaaS vendor rarely has one supervisor; instead it faces data protection authorities, certification auditors, card brands and customer security reviews at once.

items: **Law in each market.** Data protection laws apply because of where data subjects or customers are, so a company headquartered in one country can carry GDPR, APPI and Privacy Act rows at the same time.
**Certification.** ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 are voluntary, but once certified, their competence and awareness clauses are audited like rules.

**Inherited duties.** A SaaS platform that holds electronic protected health information for a US covered entity is a business associate under HIPAA; one that stores or transmits cardholder data is a PCI DSS service provider.

blocks.text: Tag each column with its type, because the type decides who checks it. The general method is in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix), and an [obligations to training map](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) keeps each column traceable to its clause.

sections.heading: Which SaaS roles should be separate rows?

blocks.text: Separate roles by the data and systems they can reach, because access is what most of the source rules turn on. A support engineer with production access to customer data carries different rows from a marketing manager with none.

See [role based training](/glossary/role-based-training) for how to assign rows by role rather than by person.

sections.heading: Which training duties apply to SaaS companies in each market?

blocks.text: The summaries below come from the library's regulation pages; each link opens the full requirement. Whether a row applies depends on where customers and data subjects are and on what the platform does.

items: **European Union.** GDPR names training only in Articles 39 and 47, but Articles 5(2) and 24 require controllers to demonstrate compliance and Articles 29 and 32(4) limit processing to instructions ([GDPR](/regulations/gdpr-staff-training-requirements)). EU AI Act Article 4, as replaced by the Digital Omnibus on AI, requires providers and deployers to take measures to support the AI literacy of staff and others using AI on their behalf ([AI Act Article 4](/regulations/eu-ai-act-ai-literacy)). Where a SaaS company is an essential or important entity, for example in digital infrastructure or ICT service management, NIS2 Article 20(2) requires management body members to follow cybersecurity training and Article 21(2)(g) requires cyber hygiene and training ([NIS2](/regulations/nis2-management-body-training)).

**United States.** Business associates must run a security awareness and training program for all workforce members, including management, under 45 CFR 164.308(a)(5) ([HIPAA](/regulations/hipaa-security-and-privacy-training)).

**Japan.** APPI Article 24 requires supervision of employees handling personal data, and the PPC General Rules Guidelines make employee education a required human security control measure, with periodic training as the illustrated method. The Act reaches foreign businesses handling personal information of individuals in Japan in connection with supplying goods or services to them ([APPI](/regulations/japan-appi-employee-training)).

**United Arab Emirates.** Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 has no express training article, but Article 7 requires appropriate technical and organizational measures and a record of who may access personal data, and Article 10 requires a Data Protection Officer with sufficient skills and knowledge in defined high risk cases ([UAE PDPL](/regulations/uae-pdpl-staff-training)).

**Australia.** The OAIC names regular staff training as an example of APP 1.2 practices and counts training as an organizational measure under APP 11.3 for organizations with annual turnover above $3 million and other covered entities ([Privacy Act](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)).

**Certifications, any market.** ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 7.2 requires determined competence with retained evidence, clause 7.3 requires awareness, and Annex A control 6.3 adds an awareness, education and training program ([ISO/IEC 27001](/regulations/iso-27001-awareness-training-requirements)). ISO/IEC 42001:2023 applies the same structure to AI management systems ([ISO/IEC 42001](/regulations/iso-iec-42001-competence-and-awareness)). PCI DSS 12.6 requires a formal security awareness program covering phishing, social engineering and acceptable use of end-user technologies ([PCI DSS](/regulations/pci-dss-security-awareness-training-requirements)).

sections.heading: Which SaaS cells carry a fixed refresh clock?

blocks.text: Very few. Most sources in a SaaS matrix require training to be appropriate, periodic or reasonable, so the company sets the interval and records the reasoning.

items: **Fixed by the source.** PCI DSS 12.6.2: review and update the awareness program at least once every 12 months. HIPAA Privacy Rule: new workforce members within a reasonable period and anyone affected by a material policy change within a reasonable period, which applies to covered entities rather than business associates.
**Risk scaled by guidance.** The PPC Guidelines say it is desirable to scale the content and frequency of education to the size of the business and the nature and volume of personal data handled.

**Not yet a clock.** A January 2025 HIPAA proposed rule would require security training at least every 12 months and within 30 days of access, but it had not been finalized as at the HIPAA page's last review. Keep it as a watch item.

**Event triggers.** New AI features, new subprocessors, new markets and policy changes should all trigger rows. The guide on [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to write those triggers down.

sections.heading: What evidence do auditors and enterprise customers expect from a SaaS firm?

blocks.text: They expect evidence that people are competent for their access, not a single completion figure. ISO/IEC 27001 auditors look for evidence of competence and effectiveness, and the HIPAA Security Rule requires documentation to be retained for six years.

items: **Competence, not attendance.** ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.2 require documented evidence of competence and evaluation of actions taken to close gaps.
**Record of who has access.** UAE PDPL Article 7(4) requires a record that includes the persons authorized to access personal data, which pairs naturally with the training record for those people.
**Accountability.** GDPR Article 5(2) means the controller must be able to demonstrate compliance, and training records are a standard part of that evidence.
**No certificate needed for AI literacy.** The European Commission says an internal record of AI literacy training and other initiatives is enough.

**Separate controls stay separate.** PCI DSS says meeting the anti-phishing mechanism requirement (5.4.1) does not meet the phishing awareness training requirement (12.6.3.1), and vice versa. The guide on [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers packaging this for a customer review.

sections.heading: Which upcoming changes should a SaaS matrix already show?

blocks.text: Several dates recorded in the library's regulation pages, as at November 2026, will change SaaS rows within the next two years. Add them as future dated rows.

items: **August 2026 onward, EU:** national market surveillance authorities supervise and enforce AI Act Article 4, with penalties set in national law.
**December 10, 2026, Australia:** automated decision making transparency obligations under the Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 commence.
**Six months after July 17, 2026, Japan:** the penalty changes in the APPI amending Act take effect, with the rest of the amendments in principle within two years of promulgation.

**December 2, 2027, EU:** AI Act Chapter III obligations for Annex III high-risk systems apply, including Article 26(2) human oversight by people with the necessary competence, training and authority, for any SaaS customer deploying such a system.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each SaaS obligation with its source type, market and clause, and links it to the learning outcome and assessment point that meet it, so a certification audit or customer questionnaire can be answered from the same structure. When a source such as the AI Act changes, affected roles are flagged. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation).

faqs.q: Does a SaaS company outside the EU need GDPR training rows?
faqs.a: If it offers services to people in the EU or monitors their behavior, the GDPR applies to it, and the accountability and security duties that imply training come with it. A processor acting for EU customers also needs staff who process personal data only on instructions, as Articles 29 and 32(4) require.

faqs.q: Do all SaaS employees need AI literacy training?
faqs.a: EU AI Act Article 4 applies to staff and others operating or using AI systems on the provider's or deployer's behalf, so anyone using general purpose AI tools at work is in scope, not only engineers. After the Digital Omnibus, the duty is to take measures that support AI literacy, without guaranteeing a set level for each individual.

faqs.q: Is a SaaS vendor covered by HIPAA training rules?
faqs.a: Only if it is a business associate, meaning it creates, receives, maintains or transmits electronic protected health information for a covered entity. Business associates must meet the Security Rule's security awareness and training standard for all workforce members. The Privacy Rule's training standard in 164.530(b) is written for covered entities.

faqs.q: Is ISO/IEC 27001 training a legal requirement?
faqs.a: No. ISO/IEC 27001 is a voluntary standard, but clause 1 says excluding any requirement in clauses 4 to 10 is not acceptable when claiming conformity, so clauses 7.2 and 7.3 are mandatory for certification. Many SaaS firms treat it as binding because customers require the certificate.
